claims.claim_text: A Jharkhand checklist reports more than 53 plants associated with Handia preparation.
claims.caution: Full plant list is not publicly visible in the accessible abstract, so it is not reconstructed.

claims.claim_text: The surveyed study reported replacement of some traditional herbs with urea, raw mahua liquor or spirit in some areas.
claims.caution: Historical source-specific observation; not generalized to current statewide practice.

claims.claim_text: Ho Ranu in West Singhbhum was reported to use Woodfordia fruticosa, Ruellia tuberosa, Andrographis paniculata, Dioscorea bulbifera roots and Madhuca longifolia bark.
Ranu composition varies among regions and tribes according to the Khunti Oraon study.
claims.caution: Preserve variation; do not define one universal recipe.

claims.claim_text: The Khunti study describes Handia as socially, culturally, economically and religiously important.
Haria was prepared from boiled rice with Bakhar in heat-sterilized earthen pots for roughly 3–4 days.
claims.caution: Do not transfer as a Jharkhand recipe.

claims.claim_text: Consumable Haria in the cited study had about 2–3% v/v alcohol and titratable acidity of 1.42%.
Yeasts and moulds peaked around day 2, while LAB and Bifidobacterium increased during the cited Haria fermentation.
The Haria study measured maltotetrose 26.18 µg/g, maltotriose 28.16 µg/g and maltose 26.94 µg/g.
Fermented material showed 82.54% DPPH radical-scavenging activity on day 4.
claims.caution: In-vitro assay; not a clinical health claim.

claims.claim_text: Twenty-nine LAB colony types were isolated; Lactobacillus fermentum KKL1 was selected and identified using 16S rRNA.
PCR-DGGE reported L. plantarum, L. brevis, Lysinibacillus sp., L. fusiformis and uncultured Bacillus groups.
The study reported lactic acid 17.63 mg/g, acetic acid 0.18 mg/g and peak phytase activity 18.93 U/g at day 4.
From 29 Bankura Haria samples, 45 dominant bacterial isolates were purified; Bifidobacterium sp. MKK4, Pediococcus lolli MKK21 and Lactobacillus sp. MKK37 were shortlisted.
Lactobacillus fermentum TIU19 isolated from Haria showed in-vitro antibacterial and antibiofilm properties in the study.
An Oraon Jharkhand food study lists Hadiya as an alcoholic fermented rice preparation obtained from home or market.
A study reported raw Handia values: carbohydrate 55 mg/100 ml, glucose 10.2 mg/100 ml, protein 162 mg/100 ml, fat 5.6 mg/100 ml and alcohol 11.3%.
claims.caution: Raw/before dilution; not equivalent to consumable diluted beverage.

claims.claim_text: Jharkhand Government's Sarhul page states Handia is distributed as prasad during Sarhul.
Khunti district's official page describes rice beer in Munda festival contexts including Karam and Sohrai.
Phulo Jhano supports women leaving hadiya/local-liquor production and sale for alternative livelihoods.
A government review reported 16,549 women identified and 7,175 connected to the campaign at that reporting time.
Jharkhand excise law defines pachwai as fermented rice, millet or other grain and liquid obtained from it.
FSSAI lists Handia as rice + ranu and Haria as rice + bhakar/dabai/mod pitha in the 2025 amendment annexure.
claims.caution: Regulatory naming; does not prove identity/equivalence.

claims.claim_text: A northern Odisha study reported 20 plant species used for Handia ranu/bakhar starter.
A West Bengal Santal Bakhar study documented 10 plant species plus one lichen.
The study reported homemade Haria ascorbic acid 15.40 mg/100 ml and flavonoids 36.67 mg/100 ml.
A 2026 Mayurbhanj Handia study used FTIR, GC-MS and ICP-OES and reported essential minerals and aroma-related compounds.
The 2026 Mayurbhanj study reported trace lead and copper in its urban Handia sample.
A 2025 North Dinajpur Haria study detected 60 HR-LCMS compounds, 37 identified.
The study reported Mipafox/N,N'-diethylthiourea signals and Enterobacter sp.
A Jharkhand community-facing account describes household variation in Ranu ingredient numbers/composition.
A Paschim Medinipur study reports 18 plant species used as ingredients of Bakhar tablets for Haria/Handia preparation.
claims.caution: Comparative evidence outside Jharkhand; does not define Jharkhand Ranu composition.

claims.claim_text: The same Bakhar study reports that 14 of the 18 documented starter plants were also used by local medicine men in folk medicine.
claims.caution: Ethnomedicinal use is a cultural report, not clinical efficacy evidence.

claims.claim_text: A Handia starter-plant study used interviews with 24 informants from 24 locations and laboratory phytochemical and antibacterial assays against enteric pathogens.
claims.caution: Comparative evidence outside Jharkhand; laboratory activity is not clinical evidence.
